body.statement: The raw fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\) is nonempty if and only if \(R\) and \(S\) have identical eigenvalues with identical multiplicities and \(A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda=B_\lambda^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). When these conditions hold, every member appears exactly once as \[W=H_1^{1/2}\left(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}Q_\lambda O_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\right)H_0^{-1/2},\qquad O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda,\quad O_\lambda\in O(m_\lambda),\] where the completion fiber of block \(\lambda\) is a torsor for \(O(k_\lambda)\) and has dimension \(k_\lambda(k_\lambda-1)/2\).
body.justification: This is the complete observable certificate and stabilizer parameterization on which every identification claim rests.
body.gap: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022, Theorem 2.1, whitens two covariance equations with known propagated noise; it does not difference out an unknown common measurement covariance or give the blockwise two-probe Gram criterion and residual stabilizers.
body.consumer: A gene-network analyst can enumerate every transition consistent with four unpaired noisy snapshot laws instead of reporting an arbitrary optimizer.
